title: The Cashback
intro: A text from your bank says you earned money back. After today, everything looks like bait.
But some messages are real. Mirage loves it when you stop trusting the honest ones.

screen.context: You paid at Meridu Store last week, using your Orrin card.

msg.text: It will show in the Orrin app under Rewards.
You do not need to do anything.

sender.label: Same thread as your bank texts
sender.lens: It sits with your past messages from the bank.
sender.why: A name alone proves nothing, but the real question is what it asks.

amount.label: A small, plain amount
amount.why: Honest offers are modest. Scams promise much more.

purchase.label: Matches your own purchase
purchase.lens: It names a shop you really paid last week.
purchase.why: It matches something you did. That is the strongest sign of an honest message.

app.label: Look in your own app
app.lens: It sends you to the app you already have.
app.why: Pointing you to your own app, not a link, is what honest banks do.

nothing.label: Asks for nothing
nothing.lens: No link, no code, no details to give.
nothing.why: A message that asks for nothing is usually honest.

actions.label: Open the Orrin app myself and look under Rewards

go_ahead.line: The app showed £4.20 cashback from the Meridu Store purchase, already added. Nothing to fear.

ignore.line: Nothing bad happened. It was a real message, and you stayed careful.

block_report.line: That was a real message. When every message looks like a scam, the real ones get lost too.
block_report.mirageSays: If you trust nothing, I win anyway.

what_if.block_report: It matched your own purchase, asked for nothing and sent you to your own app. That calm is what real messages look like.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring was safe. Recognising a real message is the skill: it asks for nothing secret and matches something you know.

golden_rule: A small reward that matches something you did, asks for nothing and sends you to your own app is usually honest.

quick_check.q: What made this cashback text honest?

options.text: It matched your own purchase, asked for nothing and sent you to your own app

quick_check.explain: Names and signs can be copied. A match with something you really did, and no request, is the real sign.

hints.nudge: What is this message actually asking you to do?

rows.k: Same thread as your bank texts

rows.v: Open your own bank app, never a link

rows.k: Does a real bank ask for codes?
